acceptance: The hard-stop bound is decided by the owner and the code, tests and docs all state and meet it.
context: Filed 2026-11-22 while closing out the run-timeout follow-ups (umbrella run-timeout-plan-20261120). Evidence was read on 2026-11-22; re-read run logs, file paths and line numbers before acting.
description:
## Problem
The run hard stop fires 30 s after the limit (`HARD_STOP_GRACE_SECONDS`, `benchbox/utils/run_deadline.py`; `hard_stop` in `benchbox/cli/run_time_limit.py`): it cancels remote work, writes the partial result, then `RunDeadline.stop_children` sends SIGTERM, waits 0.2 s and sends SIGKILL, then exits 124. The site docs say "If the command has not stopped 30 seconds after the limit, BenchBox writes that result and exits." The new test in `tests/unit/utils/test_process_group_term_ignoring_children.py` (#4446) could only assert exit within limit + 30 s + 2 s, because export and the 0.2 s TERM-to-KILL wait come after the 30 s. So "exits by limit + 30 s" is not guaranteed; "starts stopping at limit + 30 s" is.

## Change
Ask the owner which contract holds, then make code, tests and docs (BenchBox `docs/operations/run-safety.md`, the decision record `_project/decisions/run-timeout-2026-11-20.md`, and the site's `reference/cli/run.md` and `usage/data-generation.md`) say the same thing. If the owner wants an exit bound, budget the export and kill wait inside the grace instead of after it, and tighten the test to limit + 30 s.

## Decision gates
- STOP and ask the owner (choice dialog): exit bound (all work done by limit + 30 s) or start bound (stopping starts at limit + 30 s, exit follows). Quote the answer verbatim on this item.
- No new default timeout anywhere, and no deadline check inside a query timer.
- Do not shorten the 25-second remote-cleanup window without the owner's decision.

## Verification rubric
Pass: docs and decision record state the chosen bound in the owner's words; a subprocess test with a SIGTERM-ignoring child asserts that bound without extra margin on macOS and on Linux (`make ci-linux`); the existing hard-stop and remote-cleanup tests still pass.
Fail: docs and behaviour still disagree, or the test needs an unexplained margin.

## Guardrails
Work in a linked worktree (`make worktree-create`), never the primary clone. Edit files with the edit tool, never by script. Heavy work (benchmarks, test tiers, UAT, generators at scale) only through `make heavy-run` or lock-taking entry points; never skip the lock, admission or watchdog; never delete anything under `~/Developer/benchmark_runs`. No live cloud run and no cloud credentials unless this item's Decision gates say the owner approved it in the current task. BenchBox imposes no default run limit: add none. No comments or docstrings in first-party code; one changelog fragment for a user-facing change. Never post a stand-in review, close and reopen a pull request to restart CI, use `--no-verify`, force-push, or rewrite an author. Arm once; a second time only after fixing the cause the refusal named. Reply on every review thread; resolve it only after the bot's review of the new head does not raise it again. Never end processes that the test runner owns; tests signal only processes they started and still own.
